title: How AI Asset Management onboards GCP organizations: prerequisites, templates, service account, network, IAM roles and errors
aliases: GCP service account private key AI Security

prose.text: {{prereq-access}} {{key-policy}} The AWS and Azure counterparts are in [[ai-security.asset-management.onboarding-aws]] and [[ai-security.asset-management.onboarding-azure]], and the product overview is in [[ai-security.asset-management]].

prose.label: APIs, scopes and the custom role.
Configuration errors.
prose.text: {{err-location-policy}} {{err-logging-bucket}} The error table gives two different fixes for the same bucket error {{divergence:active-bucket-delete-fix}}.{{err-provider-lock}} {{err-network-mismatch}} {{err-misc}} {{err-connectivity}}

checks.do: Whether the Disable service account key creation policy reads Not enforced for the project before creating the service account key.
That a GCP project added to the monitoring scope cannot be removed from it; stopping monitoring means deleting the project from the AI Security organization.
Whether the GCP service account was deleted when all onboarded projects show Needs Attention.

service-account-deleted.statement: If the GCP service account is accidentally deleted, AI Security's access is impacted and all onboarded projects in the organization move to Needs Attention; updating the service account details restores access.

quotes: While onboarding a GCP organization, a service account is created within the GCP organization.

If the service account is accidentally deleted, AI Security's access to the onboarded organization is impacted, and all the onboarded projects within the organization move to the Needs Attention state.
To restore access, you must update the service account details.

service-account-update-flow.statement: Updating the GCP service account means pasting the JSON output into Generated JSON in the Update Service Account window, then running the GCP Onboarding template from the Roles and Templates tab; after deployment access is restored and projects return to Successfully Configured. It needs an Administrator role or any role with permission to add accounts.

quotes: You must be assigned either an Administrator role or any role with permission to add accounts in the Zscaler Admin Console.
In the Update Service Account window, paste the JSON output into the Generated JSON text field.
On the Roles and Templates tab, download and run the GCP Onboarding template:
After the template is successfully deployed, AI Security's access to the GCP organization is restored, and the onboarded projects move to the Successfully Configured state.

private-key.statement: The GCP service account private key is generated in JSON format when the tree discovery template is applied; it can be updated at any time if keys need updating or have expired, by uploading the downloaded JSON key, and AI Security validates it against the service account and shows an error if it is invalid or does not match.

quotes: During the GCP account onboarding process, a private key is generated in JSON format when you apply the tree discovery template
If your service account keys need to be updated or have expired, you can update your service account key at any time.
AI Security validates the updated private key by verifying it against the service account.
If the private key is invalid, or it does not match the service account, an error is displayed.
upload the downloaded JSON file to the AI Security Admin Portal

private-key-perm.statement: Updating the private key needs an Administrator role or any role with permission to add accounts, and a service account private key downloaded in JSON format from the Google Cloud Console.

quotes: You must be assigned either an Administrator role or any role with permission to add accounts in the AI Security Admin Portal.
Download a private key for your service account in JSON format from the Google Cloud Console.

err-location-policy.statement: The GCP error 403 LOCATION_POLICY_VIOLATED (permission denied on locations/REGION) while creating a subnetwork is fixed by terraform destroy, changing the orchestrator in the Admin Portal, deploying the new GCP template and ensuring the region has the necessary permissions.

quotes: Error creating Subnetwork: googleapi: Error 403: Permission denied on 'locations/[REGION]'

Run the terraform destroy command to purge the template. Change the orchestrator in the AI Security Admin Portal. Download and deploy the new GCP template. Ensure that the selected region has the necessary permissions.

err-logging-bucket.statement: For the GCP error 400 'Only buckets in state ACTIVE can be deleted', the error table says to restore the bucket on the Logs Storage page and run terraform destroy; the error 'Buckets must be in an ACTIVE state to be modified' is resolved by restoring the log bucket, running terraform destroy and rerunning the template.

quotes: In the Google Cloud console, go to the Logs Storage page. Restore the bucket for which the error is occurring. To learn more, refer to the Google Cloud documentation. Run the terraform destroy command to purge the template.
Error deleting Logging Bucket Config "[BUCKET_LOCATION]/[BUCKET_NAME]": googleapi: Error 400: Only buckets in state ACTIVE can be deleted
Buckets must be in an ACTIVE state to be modified
Restore the log bucket. Run the terraform destroy command to purge the template. Rerun the template.

err-provider-lock.statement: The Terraform error that locked provider hashicorp/google 5.40.0 does not match constraint 6.0.0 is fixed with terraform init -upgrade, which updates the locked provider version to match the configured version.

quotes: locked provider registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/google 5.40.0 does not match configured version constraint 6.0.0
Run the terraform init -upgrade command to allow the selection of new versions. This command updates the locked provider version to match the configured version.

err-network-mismatch.statement: The managed group instances error that networks in new and old network interfaces must be the same is due to a mismatch between old and new network interfaces; the fix is to stop the VM, delete its template and the orchestrator instance group, then redeploy the template.

quotes: Cause: The issue is due to a mismatch between the network interfaces specified in the old and new configurations for the managed instance group.
Stop the VM instance and delete the associated template. Delete the instance group. Download and redeploy the template.
Identify and open the orchestrator instance group to which the VM is integrated.

err-misc.statement: A GCP Service Networking error because a peering operation is in progress is fixed by rerunning the template; an instance template error (specified network resource does not exist) is fixed by verifying the network resource, updating the reference and deploying the new GCP template.

quotes: There is a peering operation in progress on the local or peer network. Try again later.
Cause: Specified network resource does not exist.
Verify the existence of the specified network resource. Update the network resource reference in the instance template configuration. Download and deploy the new GCP template.
Cause: Unable to remove the Service Networking Connection because of an ongoing operation. | Rerun the template. |

err-connectivity.statement: The local-exec provisioner error in the test-connectivity module (Connectivity test failed) is resolved by rerunning the template; the check passes only if the gcloud connectivity test reachabilityDetails.result is REACHABLE.

quotes: if [[ "$connection_status" == "REACHABLE" ]]; then echo "Connectivity test succeeded" else echo "Connectivity test failed" exit 1 fi
Output: Connectivity test failed | Rerun the template. |
--format="get(reachabilityDetails.result)"

prereq-access.statement: GCP organization onboarding needs Super Admin access to the Google Admin console, a GCP Organization Administrator role and an owner role, Terraform CLI v1.7.5 or later to run Terraform on a Windows system, and a GCP project with the required roles linked to a billing account to deploy the orchestrator template.

quotes: You must have Super Admin access to the Google Admin console.
You must have a GCP Organization Administrator role and an owner role.
Terraform CLI v1.7.5 or later to run the Terraform on a Windows system.
Identify a GCP project that has the required roles and which is linked to a billing account to deploy the orchestrator template.

custom-role.statement: Creating the custom role in the Google Admin console is optional; if skipped, AI Security cannot gain read-only access to user, group and domain resource data. The role holds DOMAIN_MANAGEMENT, GROUPS_RETRIEVE and USERS_RETRIEVE privileges, read-only for domain, group and user data.

quotes: This is an optional step. If skipped, AI Security cannot gain read-only access to this resource data.

{ "roleName": "role_name", "rolePrivileges": [ { "privilegeName": "DOMAIN_MANAGEMENT", "serviceId": "00haapch16h1ysv" }, { "privilegeName": "GROUPS_RETRIEVE", "serviceId": "00haapch16h1ysv" }, { "privilegeName": "USERS_RETRIEVE", "serviceId": "00haapch16h1ysv" } ] }
| User | Read | To collect the user data |
| Group | Read | To collect the group and member data |
| Domain Management | Read | To collect domain resources |

key-policy.statement: By default the Disable service account key creation policy prevents creating a service account key, so it must be overridden for the project, and its status must read Not enforced.

quotes: By default, the disable service account key creation policy prevents you from creating a service account key.
Override the disable service account key creation policy for the project where you want to create the service account.
Ensure the status of Disable service account key creation policy is set to Not enforced.

api-scope.statement: The required GCP APIs are scoped by project type: for example admin.googleapis.com and cloudasset.googleapis.com for Tree Discovery and Target projects; networkmanagement.googleapis.com (required for BYON) for the Orchestrator; aiplatform.googleapis.com for the Target project only.

quotes: | admin.googleapis.com | Discover Google Workspace account resources | Tree Discovery, Target |
| cloudasset.googleapis.com | Discover the history and inventory of Google Cloud resources | Tree Discovery, Target |
| networkmanagement.googleapis.com | Check connections between virtual private cloud (VPC) network and AI Security. It is required for BYON | Orchestrator |
| aiplatform.googleapis.com | Interact with Google's unified artificial intelligence and machine learning platform for AI Security to scan the AI models for vulnerabilities | Target |

api-compute.statement: compute.googleapis.com applies to Orchestrator and Target projects, needs the project linked to billing, and must be enabled on the target project before notebooks.googleapis.com (Vertex AI resources) can be enabled; serviceusage.googleapis.com and iam.googleapis.com apply to Tree Discovery, Orchestrator and Target.

quotes: | compute.googleapis.com | Discover compute resources and perform compute-related operations This is required to enable notebooks.googleapis.com and compute resources on the target project. | Orchestrator, Target To enable this API, the project must be linked to billing. |
To enable this API, the project must be linked to billing.
compute.googleapis.com must be enabled on the target project to enable notebooks.googleapis.com.
| serviceusage.googleapis.com | Consume quota for a project | Tree Discovery, Orchestrator, Target |
| iam.googleapis.com | Discover identity and access control for Google Cloud resources | Tree Discovery, Orchestrator, Target |

oauth-scopes.statement: Zscaler AI Security uses six OAuth scopes for GCP API authentication: cloud-platform, userinfo.email, and read-only admin.directory user, group, group.member and domain.

quotes: Zscaler AI Security leverages the following OAuth scopes for API authentication:
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.email
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.user.readonly
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.group.readonly
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.group.member.readonly
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.domain.readonly

org-details.statement: GCP role and service account names may contain only alphabetic characters, numbers, hyphens and underscores; the Organization Name is validated against the Organization ID on the GCP console, and up to 30 notification emails can be added.

quotes: The role and service account names must contain only alphabetic characters, numbers, hyphens ("-"), and underscores ("_").
This organization name will be validated with the Organization ID on the GCP console.
You can add up to 30 email addresses to receive notifications about the issues.

network-config.statement: GCP onboarding offers Zscaler or Custom network configuration, Custom is selected by default, and changing it resets existing configurations; Custom requires VPC and Subnet selflinks.

quotes: Zscaler: Use Zscaler resources to deploy the orchestrator and monitoring scope.
Custom: Use your organization's resources to deploy the orchestrator and monitoring scope.
By default, the custom configuration is selected.
Changing the network configuration resets the existing configurations.
VPC Selflink: Enter the selflink of the VPC network where you want to deploy the orchestrator.
Subnet Selflink: Enter the selflink of the subnet within the selected VPC where you want to deploy the orchestrator.

monitoring-scope.statement: GCP monitoring scope: selecting the main project group scans all its projects, Autodetection includes new projects added later, all projects in a management group share one business unit, and a default is assigned.

quotes: Select the main project group if all projects under that group must be scanned.
Select Autodetection if you want AI Security to automatically include and scan new projects that are added to the management group in the future.
All projects in that management group are assigned to the same business unit.
A default business unit is assigned to the management groups.

evidence-storage.statement: GCP evidence storage is a Custom Bucket (existing bucket, selected by default) or a Zscaler Managed Bucket that AI Security creates in the orchestrator project to hold evidence snippets.

quotes: By default, the Custom Bucket storage type is selected.
You can use an existing bucket to configure evidence data.
AI Security creates a new bucket in the orchestrator project to upload the snippet of evidence data.
Zscaler Managed Bucket

template-deploy.statement: The GCP onboarding template prompts for the regions to monitor and creates scanning resources only there, and terraform apply takes enable_test_connectivity=true or false to deploy with network analysis enabled or disabled; AI Security validates the deployment every hour.

quotes: AI Security creates resources required for data scanning only in these specified regions.
terraform apply -var=‘enable_test_connectivity=true’
terraform apply -var=‘enable_test_connectivity=false’
AI Security validates the template deployment every hour by checking the roles that are created and permissions granted.
evidence.after: - c. Initialize the GCP onboarding template.

terraform-api-check.statement: Terraform verifies that all the required APIs are enabled and, if any is missing, shows an error message prompting you to enable the APIs.

quotes: Terraform verifies that all the required APIs are enabled. If any API is missing, an error message is displayed prompting you to enable the APIs and then continue with the verification.

monitoring-scope-add-only.statement: GCP projects added to the monitoring scope cannot be removed; to stop monitoring a project it must be deleted from the AI Security organization. Managing scope needs the Administrator role or any role with the Configure Monitoring Scope permission.

quotes: After a project has been added to the monitoring scope, you cannot remove it from the monitoring scope.
If you want to stop monitoring a project, you need to delete the project from the AI Security organization.
Be assigned either an Administrator role or any role with the Configure Monitoring Scope permission in the AI Security Admin Portal.

template-regions-prompt.statement: When running the GCP onboarding Terraform template, terraform plan and terraform apply prompt for regions as a list in the format ["region name1", "region name2", ...]; AI Security creates resources required for data scanning only in the specified regions.

quotes: For Enter a value, enter the regions where you want AI Security to monitor and scan data in the following format:
["region name1", "region name2", "region name3", and so on.]
ai-security creates resources required for data scanning only in these specified regions.
For Enter a value, enter the regions where you want to deploy the template in the following format:
["region name1", "region name2", "region name3", and so on.]

orchestrator-change-log-bucket.statement: When changing the GCP orchestrator project, the Log Bucket Name must be unique (otherwise AI Security shows an error); the bucket stores the activity logs of the target projects and is created while deploying the onboarding template.

quotes: Log Bucket Name: Enter a unique name for the log bucket. This log bucket stores the activity logs of the target projects.
The log bucket is created while deploying the onboarding template. The name must be unique, otherwise AI Security shows an error message.

orchestrator-change-purge-validation.statement: Before running the GCP template on a new orchestrator project, the template deployed on the existing orchestrator is purged with terraform destroy; AI Security validates the deployment every hour by checking created roles and granted permissions, and starts scanning the onboarded projects once the template is deployed.

quotes: Before running the template on the new orchestrator subscription, purge the template that was previously deployed on the existing orchestrator by running the terraform destroy command.
AI Security validates the template deployment every hour by checking the roles that are created and permissions granted.
After the template is successfully deployed, the AI Security begins the data scan for the onboarded projects

iam-discovery-service-account.statement: The GCP Discovery Service Account is used by AI Security to discover resources in the GCP projects and to instruct the Local Scanner Platform to perform scan-related instructions; its managed roles include Cloud Asset Viewer, Security Reviewer, Organization Policy Viewer and Folder Viewer.

quotes: This service account is used by AI Security to discover resources in the GCP projects and to instruct Local Scanner Platform to perform scan-related instructions.
Organization Policy Viewer
Folder Viewer
Security Reviewer
Cloud Asset Viewer

iam-orchestrator-log-sink.statement: The GCP Orchestrator Service Account is used by the orchestrator instance to perform scan and management operations; its logging.sinks.get, logging.sinks.list and logging.sinks.update permissions are scoped to the GCP Organisation to update the org log sink for buckets incremental scans.

quotes: This service account is used by the orchestrator instance to perform scan and management operations.
| logging.sinks.get | GCP Organisation | To update Zscaler AI Security org log sink for buckets incremental scans |
| logging.sinks.list | GCP Organisation | To update Zscaler AI Security org log sink for buckets incremental scans |
| logging.sinks.update | GCP Organisation | To update Zscaler AI Security org log sink for buckets incremental scans |

iam-scanner-and-target.statement: The GCP Scanner Service Account is used by the scanner instance to perform scan-related tasks and its permission table lists logging.logEntries.list and secretmanager.versions.access with scope Monitored Projects; the Target Role service account performs scan-related tasks on data stores.

quotes: This service account is used by the scanner instance to perform scan-related tasks.
The service account with this role is used to perform scan-related tasks on data stores.
| logging.logEntries.list | Monitored Projects | To list log entries from log views |
| secretmanager.versions.access | Monitored Projects | To access Zscaler AI Security secret version |
evidence.after: This service account is used by the scanner instance to perform scan-related tasks.

iam-bigquery.statement: Scanning GCP BigQuery projects needs, among others, bigquery.datasets.get, bigquery.jobs.create, bigquery.models.getData and bigquery.tables.getData on Monitored Projects.

quotes: The following permissions are required to scan GCP BigQuery projects:
| bigquery.datasets.get | Monitored Projects | To read the metadata of BigQuery datasets |
| bigquery.jobs.create | Monitored Projects | To run BigQuery jobs |
| bigquery.models.getData | Monitored Projects | To read data from BigQuery ML models for scanning |
| bigquery.tables.getData | Monitored Projects | To read the contents of BigQuery tables for scanning |

network-vpc-topology.statement: The GCP network page's introduction says a custom network needs a Control Plane VPC created only in the primary region where the orchestrator runs and a Worker Plane VPC in all the regions where the resources exist, both in the orchestrator project, with non-overlapping CIDR ranges; its steps build the worker plane as one VPC with an added subnet per additional region and create Cloud NAT for the new subnet and region.

quotes: You must configure a custom network in your organization by creating the following virtual private cloud (VPC) in the orchestrator project:
Control Plane VPC: Create this VPC only in the primary region where the orchestrator is going to run.
Worker Plane VPC: Create this VPC in all the regions where the resources exist.
Ensure that both control and worker plane VPC do not have overlapping Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR).
To add multiple subnets in different regions, click ADD SUBNET and repeat these steps for each additional subnet as required.
After creating the worker plane VPC, create and configure the Cloud NAT gateway resources for the new subnet and region in the worker plane.

network-db-firewall.statement: The worker plane firewall rule allow-db-outbound-rule allows outbound communication from the scanner to GCP Cloud SQL instances on ports 3306, 5432 and 1433.

quotes: Name: Enter allow-db-outbound-rule.
To add a rule to allow outbound communication from the scanner to GCP Cloud SQL instances:

network-private-service-access.statement: Private service access in the worker plane VPC is used for scanning GCP Cloud SQL instances; it allocates an IP range named private-service-access-ip-range with Automatic range and prefix length 16, and Google then adds peering from the worker plane VPC to servicenetworking.

quotes: This is used for scanning GCP Cloud SQL instances.
Name: Enter private-service-access-ip-range.
IP range: Select Automatic.
Prefix length: Enter 16.
Google adds peering from the worker plane VPC to servicenetworking.

network-peering-status.statement: The peering status in the control plane VPC is Inactive after the peering is added there; after successful configuration of the peering the status is Active for both the control plane VPC and the worker plane VPC.

quotes: The peering status in the control plane VPC is Inactive.
After successful configuration of the peering, the peering status is updated to Active for both the control plane VPC and worker plane VPC.

network-cloud-nat.statement: Cloud NAT is a region-specific and network-specific resource that must be created for each combination; a Control Plane NAT Gateway is created, and the steps are repeated for a Worker Plane Cloud NAT Gateway for each region where data stores are present.

quotes: Gateway name: Enter a name for the Control Plane NAT Gateway.
The Cloud NAT Gateway is a region-specific and network-specific resource that must be created for each combination.
Repeat the steps for the Worker Plane Cloud NAT Gateway, for each region where data stores are present, selecting the Worker Plane VPC Network in Cloud Router options.

active-bucket-delete-fix.summary: Two rows of the GCP configuration-issues error table carry the error 'Only buckets in state ACTIVE can be deleted' with different resolutions.

quotes: In the Google Cloud console, go to the Logs Storage page. Restore the bucket for which the error is occurring. To learn more, refer to the Google Cloud documentation. Run the terraform destroy command to purge the template.

positions.says: Restore the bucket on the Logs Storage page, then run terraform destroy.

quotes: Attempt to delete a Logging Bucket Config that is not in the ACTIVE state.
Change the orchestrator in the AI Security Admin Portal. Download and deploy the new GCP template.
evidence.after: Stop the VM instance and delete the associated template. Delete the instance group. Download and redeploy the template.

positions.says: For an attempt to delete a Logging Bucket Config not in the ACTIVE state, change the orchestrator in the Admin Portal and deploy the new GCP template.

active-bucket-delete-fix.impact: The page does not say which fix applies to which situation, so the resolution for this error cannot be chosen from the page alone.
